repo_model.summary: This is a RelBench generic-search candidate workspace: main.py loads a configured sanitized task and emits validation/test NumPy predictions, while the provided evaluation grader runs the candidate, validates predictions, scores official validation metrics, and archives full runs.

entrypoints.how_to_run: python main.py --debug for the cheap contract run, or python main.py for the full candidate run

where_to_edit.role: Primary candidate implementation: load the task, build features/models, generate validation and test predictions, and save the required artifacts.
Optional contract-aware task-loading, prediction-saving, temporal-safety, and recommendation-metric helpers.

claims.statement: The candidate reads RELBENCH_DATASET and RELBENCH_TASK from the environment, resolves the RelBench task with download=False, and sizes outputs from the validation and test tables.

evidence.description: Reads the dataset name from the environment

claims.statement: Prediction generation dispatches by task family: recommendations receive tiled rank IDs, binary classification receives 0.5 probabilities, multiclass classification receives uniform class scores, and other tasks receive the training target median.

evidence.description: Uses the training table for the fallback task family

claims.statement: Candidate predictions are written as NumPy files under KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; ordinary runs write validation and test predictions, while rolling ticks intentionally write only test predictions for later harness assembly.

evidence.description: Writes validation predictions only outside rolling mode
Assembles tick predictions into final split vectors

claims.statement: kapso_datasets.common provides a TaskContext containing the dataset, task, database, and train/validation/test tables, plus contract-aware prediction saving and a temporal-safety guard.

evidence.description: Defines saving of both prediction files

claims.statement: The grader runs main.py in an isolated child subprocess, loads the resulting files, computes RelBench validation metrics, checks the configured primary metric, and archives full-fidelity runs with candidate code and metadata.

evidence.description: Loads the configured task for scoring
Snapshots candidate code into the archive

claims.statement: Each normal evaluation run must produce val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy with rows positionally aligned to the task validation and test tables; validation predictions must be out-of-sample.

evidence.description: Requires both prediction files after every run
Requires validation predictions to be out-of-sample

claims.statement: Non-recommendation outputs are one-dimensional per-row predictions except multiclass outputs, which are shaped (N, C); values must be finite, and binary predictions must lie in [0, 1].

evidence.description: Specifies binary, regression, and multiclass output formats

claims.statement: Recommendation predictions must be integer arrays shaped (N, K), containing ranked distinct destination IDs in the valid destination range.

evidence.description: Defines recommendation dtype, shape, ranking, uniqueness, and ID range

claims.statement: The search score of record is the configured official validation primary metric; test metrics are private and test labels are absent from the sanitized cache.

evidence.description: Defines the official validation primary metric as the search score
States that test labels are physically absent
Places the primary validation metric in the manifest score

claims.statement: Features derived from temporal tables must not use rows later than the prediction seed time; the provided guard raises on any such row.

evidence.description: Counts rows after the seed time

claims.statement: The fast evaluation command runs main.py --debug, completes the full official validation scoring, and does not reduce the scored validation item set.

evidence.description: States that both fidelities score the complete validation split
Warns not to subsample validation rows

claims.statement: After writing predictions, run kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py; success reports OK for both splits and then prints that all checks passed.
main.py is explicitly a seeded trivial baseline rather than a real solution; its current task-family outputs are constant or rank-based defaults.

evidence.description: Identifies the file as a baseline candidate
Instructs the user to replace the baseline

claims.statement: The current candidate does not implement a separate cheap debug build: --debug only changes the diagnostic text in the final print, while prediction generation is otherwise unchanged.

evidence.description: Uses --debug only in the diagnostic field

claims.statement: In rolling snapshots, an empty validation table is the signal for rolling mode, main.py skips writing a per-tick validation file, and the grader requires per-tick test predictions before assembling final split vectors.

evidence.description: Documents empty validation tables in rolling snapshots
Maps the empty validation snapshot to zero validation rows
Sets rolling mode from the empty validation count
Conditionally omits validation output in rolling mode
Requires each rolling tick to write test predictions
Builds final vectors from tick outputs

claims.statement: The prediction checker warns rather than fails when recommendation IDs are out of range or duplicated, so a passing checker does not guarantee valid recommendation quality.
The candidate and evaluation suite require Python with relbench and numpy installed; main.py imports NumPy and RelBench task/base APIs directly.

evidence.description: States that configuration is supplied by the handler
Lists relbench and numpy as required installed dependencies

claims.statement: Execution depends on handler-provided RELBENCH_DATASET, RELBENCH_TASK, RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR, and KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR; the grader additionally requires the primary metric, work directory, and timeout environment variables.

evidence.description: Documents dataset and task environment variables
Documents primary metric and work directory variables
Documents debug and full timeout variables

book.summary: This is a RelBench generic-search candidate workspace: main.py loads a configured sanitized task and emits validation/test NumPy predictions, while the provided evaluation grader runs the candidate, validates predictions, scores official validation metrics, and archives full runs.

toc.title: Architecture
toc.one_liner: Task loading, task-family prediction generation, artifact writing, and isolated evaluation are separated between the candidate and provided harness.

toc.title: Entrypoints
toc.one_liner: Run the candidate directly for debug/full modes or invoke the provided grader for official evaluation.

toc.title: Where to edit
toc.one_liner: Replace the seeded baseline in main.py; reuse the starter helpers when useful.

toc.title: Invariants
toc.one_liner: Prediction files, shapes, alignment, leakage rules, and scoring semantics are fixed by the evaluation contract.

toc.title: Testing
toc.one_liner: Use the fast grader mode and the prediction self-check before relying on official scores.

toc.title: Gotchas
toc.one_liner: The checked-in candidate is intentionally trivial, debug mode is not cheaper yet, and rolling/checker behavior has important exceptions.

toc.title: Dependencies
toc.one_liner: The runtime depends on Python with RelBench and NumPy, plus handler-provided environment configuration.
